games.title: Habitat Homes
games.skillName: Matching animals to the habitats that suit them
games.statutoryRequirement: Identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited and describe how different habitats provide for the basic needs of different kinds of animals and plants, and how they depend on each other
games.instruction: Tap the habitat where each animal lives.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about whether the animal needs to keep warm, keep cool or swim, then try again.

questions.ask: A snowy owl
A camel
A shark
A squirrel
An arctic fox
A fennec fox
A jellyfish
A badger

games.title: Living Check
games.skillName: Telling alive, dead and never-alive things apart
games.statutoryRequirement: Explore and compare the differences between things that are living, dead, and things that have never been alive
games.hint: Not quite. Ask yourself: is it alive now, was it once alive, or was it never alive?

questions.ask: Which one has never been alive?
Which one is alive now?
Which one was once alive but is dead now?
Which one is NOT a living thing?
Which of these was never part of a plant or an animal?
Which one is alive and can grow?
Three of these were once alive. Which one never was?
Which one is living? The others are dead or were never alive.

games.title: Plant Power
games.skillName: Knowing how plants grow and what they need
games.statutoryRequirement: Observe and describe how seeds and bulbs grow into mature plants, and find out and describe how plants need water, light and a suitable temperature to grow and stay healthy
games.instruction: Is it true or false? Tap your answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what a plant needs to grow and stay healthy, then try again.

questions.ask: Plants need water to grow and stay healthy.
A plant will stay healthy if you keep it in a dark cupboard.
A small seed can grow into a big plant.
A daffodil can grow from a bulb.
Most plants grow best when it is freezing cold.
Plants need light to grow well.
A bulb is a kind of animal egg.
Big plants never need water.

games.title: Healthy Me
games.skillName: Knowing what animals need and how to stay healthy
games.statutoryRequirement: Find out about and describe the basic needs of animals, including humans, for survival (water, food and air), and describe the importance for humans of exercise, eating the right amounts of different types of food, and hygiene
games.instruction: Tap the word that fills the gap.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what keeps a body alive, healthy and strong, then try again.

questions.ask: We wash our hands to get rid of ___.
Running and jumping are kinds of ___.
All animals need food, water and ___ to stay alive.
We should eat lots of fruit and ___ every day.
Brushing your teeth is part of good ___.
Exercise makes your heart and ___ stronger.
We should only eat a small amount of ___ food.
Fish need to live in ___.

games.title: Growing Up
games.skillName: Seeing how young animals grow into adults
games.statutoryRequirement: Notice that animals, including humans, have offspring which grow into adults
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what the young animal will look like when it is a grown-up.

questions.ask: Egg → Chick → ?
Frogspawn → Tadpole → Froglet → ?
Baby → Toddler → Child → Teenager → ?
Egg → Caterpillar → Chrysalis → ?
A kitten grows up. Kitten → ?
A lamb grows up. Lamb → ?
A foal grows up. Foal → ?
Egg → Duckling → ?

games.title: Minibeast Mystery
games.statutoryRequirement: Identify and name a variety of plants and animals in their habitats, including microhabitats
games.instruction: Listen to the clues and tap the answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about where the creature lives and what its body looks like.

questions.ask: I hide under damp logs. I have a hard grey shell and 14 legs. What am I?
I wriggle through the soil. I have no legs and I eat dead leaves. What am I?
I spin a web in the corner of a shed. I have eight legs. What am I?
I carry a shell on my back and leave a slimy trail. What am I?
I am red with black spots. I eat greenfly on leaves. What am I?
I am a tiny, dark, damp home under a log for minibeasts. What am I?
I live in a hive and make honey from flower nectar. What am I?
I have six legs. I live with thousands of others in a nest underground. What am I?

games.title: Shape Changers
games.skillName: Predicting how squashing and stretching change shapes
games.statutoryRequirement: Find out how the shapes of solid objects made from some materials can be changed by squashing, bending, twisting and stretching
games.instruction: Tap what you think will happen.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about how the material feels and what your hands are doing to it.

questions.ask: What happens when you squash a ball of play dough?
What will happen if you stretch an elastic band?
What will happen if you let go of a stretched elastic band?
What happens when you bend a metal paperclip?
What happens when you twist a wet cloth?
What will happen if you try to bend a brick with your hands?
What will happen if you squash a sponge and then let go?
What will happen if you twist a pipe cleaner?

games.title: Food Chain Words
games.skillName: Using words for food chains and habitats
games.statutoryRequirement: Describe how animals obtain their food from plants and other animals, using the idea of a simple food chain, and identify and name different sources of food
games.hint: Not quite. Think about who eats what, and where living things live, then try again.

questions.ask: A diagram that shows what eats what.
A place where an animal can hide and stay safe and dry.
Something that was once alive but is not alive now.
The place where a plant or animal lives.
A very small habitat, like under a stone.
Living things at the start of a food chain. They make their own food.
Where an animal gets its food from.
The young of an animal or plant.

games.title: Material Match
games.skillName: Choosing the best material for a job
games.statutoryRequirement: Identify and compare the suitability of a variety of everyday materials, including wood, metal, plastic, glass, brick, rock, paper and cardboard for particular uses
games.instruction: Tap the best material for the job.
games.hint: Not quite. Does the job need something strong, see-through, waterproof or easy to fold?

questions.ask: Which material is best for a window you can see through?
Which material is best for building a strong house wall?
Which material is best for a saucepan that goes on a hot cooker?
Which material is best for writing a letter on?
Which material is best for a raincoat to keep you dry?
Which material is best for a light box to post a parcel in?
Which material is best for a strong garden path?
Which material comes from trees and is best for a cricket bat?

games.title: Plant Detectives
games.skillName: Using simple equipment and tests to study plants
games.statutoryRequirement: Observing closely, using simple equipment; performing simple tests; gathering and recording data to help in answering questions; using their observations and ideas to suggest answers to questions
games.hint: Not quite. Think about which tool or test would really help you find the answer.

questions.ask: Which would you use to measure how tall your bean plant grows?
Which would you use to look closely at a tiny seed?
Which would you use to find out how warm it is next to your plant?
Which would you use to give each plant the same amount of water?
One plant is in the light, one is in a dark cupboard. What should stay the same?
Your plant in the dark cupboard went pale and weak. What does this tell you?
How could you record how tall your plant is each day?
Which would you use to count how many days a seed takes to sprout?
